title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (as-of 2026-09-30) — the series' only 10 AM edition, and the only one that has ever been materially late
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct by this event's own initial research 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) — its 2026 December row reads 15 | 15 | 31, and the 31 was placed in the fourth column, headed 'Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter', by parsing table cells by index rather than by reading the row as prose. The note block gives the rule: 'The release dates are the last business day of each quarter (March, June, September, and December).' A SECOND Treasury primary re-fetched the same session (home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system-home-page/tic-forms-instructions/us-gross-external-debt, HTTP 200, 174,127 bytes) states the time and singles this edition out: 'Releases are made at 4 PM in Washington D.C. on the last business day of March, June, and September, and at 10 AM on the last business day of December.' Corroborated mechanically: 2026-12-31 is a Thursday and December 2026's last business day, recomputed from 5 U.S.C. 6103 rules rather than a holiday list, and the rule reproduces 54 of 59 genuine first-vintage publications at offset +0 across all 134 archived Table A vintages re-fetched this session. Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this session per the sibling precedents (tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30, -2027-03-31, tic-annual-survey-prelim-2027-02-26): the estimate ground both proposals cited was this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and that is cleared by the event's own session re-fetching both pages. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's never-assessed initial research after reading BOTH proposals that created it (from-tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 and from-tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-03-31, now shadowed and left in place). WHAT `confirmed` COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it describes the published schedule only. This is the edition of the series that carries essentially all of its schedule risk, and the risk is stated here rather than hidden by the label. Split by edition across the 134 vintages, March is 15/15 at offset +0, September 14/14, June 13/15 and December 12/15 — and December owns BOTH of the only two slips in fifteen years longer than two days: 2019-01-31 at +31 (the release date sat inside the 35-day funding lapse of 2018-12-22 to 2019-01-25) and 2026-01-16 at +16, flagged '16 (delayed)' in the gross-external-debt column of Treasury's own 2026 table. THE STRUCTURAL REASON IS SPECIFIC TO THIS EDITION: the December edition is the only one of the four whose reference-quarter-close to release window (2026-09-30 -> 2026-12-31) always contains October 1, the federal fiscal-year boundary and the one date on which a US funding lapse can begin by statute. Both slips follow a long lapse in that window; the 16-day 2013 lapse in the same window produced no slip, so the ledger's registered claim is duration-conditioned, not lapse-conditioned. THE MECHANISM IS LIVE: cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (estimate, high) funds agencies only THROUGH 2026-12-11, so a lapse would begin 00:00 on 2026-12-12 and this release would fall on its day 20 — the 2018 configuration, which produced +31. THE OTHER THING THAT MAKES THIS EDITION DIFFERENT: it is the only one published at 10 AM ET, inside the US cash session, so the 'publishes after the close' ground every sibling ledger rested its stand-aside on does not apply here. The ledger runs the same-session tape test that fact demands and returns a null on two controls (4.21bp, n=14, max 7bp ever, vs 3.89bp for all sessions, p=0.552). Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: no accompanying press release at all (Treasury states this on the release-dates page), data a quarter stale at print, and no house playbook keyed to a macro release. Corridor is 26 tracked events over +-5 days, on a year-end session carrying Russell style capping and the S&P select-sector secondary reweight. Nothing here licenses an entry.
